title: Equivariant commutative algebras over an algebra coaction
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a commutative Hopf $k$-algebra. Let $E$ be a commutative $k$-algebra with an algebra coaction $\rho_E:E\to E\otimes_k C$ in the sense of [def-sfb-hopf-action-module-data]. An equivariant $E$-algebra is a commutative $k$-algebra $D$, an algebra coaction $\rho_D:D\to D\otimes_k C$ in that same sense, and a $k$-algebra map $j:E\to D$ satisfying $\rho_Dj=(j\otimes1)\rho_E$. Morphisms are $k$-algebra maps $f:D\to D\prime$ satisfying $fj=j\prime$ and $\rho_{D\prime}f=(f\otimes1)\rho_D$; identity and composition are the underlying algebra maps. There is no finite-generation restriction on $D$. The forgetful functor retains the underlying commutative ring. The invariant ring is the actual subring $D^C=\{d\in D:\rho_D(d)=d\otimes1\}$. The algebra carriers lie in any common ambient universe containing $k,C,E$.
